script.title: Who Actually Makes Your Coca-Cola? #shorts

segments.text: Coca-Cola doesn’t actually make your cold drink.
segments.broll: close up soda glass pouring ice
broll_alt: cold drink glass bubbling slow motion
person drinking soda can close up

segments.text: In India, most Coke, Sprite, and Thums Up come from a bottling company called HCCB.
The American parent company only sells the secret syrup formula, completely dodging heavy factory and transport costs.
HCCB does the hard work: purifying water, packing glass bottles, and trucking crates to millions of kirana stores.
Now, HCCB is going public, filing papers to sell nearly one hundred crore shares.
It’s a low-margin game, but owning the chilled fridge space in Indian heat prints serious money.
Not financial advice, but next time you crack open a chilled bottle, remember...

script.description: Ever wondered why Coca-Cola doesn't manufacture its own soda in India? Here is the secret bottling model behind Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages (HCCB) and its mega IPO. #business #ipo #money

facts_to_verify.claim: Coca-Cola India bottler HCCB has filed for an IPO with 99.75 crore shares up for sale.
Coca-Cola operates via a bottling franchise model selling syrup concentrate while bottlers manage production and distribution.

script.chosen_candidate: Coca-Cola's Indian bottling business files for IPO; 99.75 crore shares up for sale - The Times of India
script.why_it_will_work: Every Indian drinks Coke or Thums Up, but almost nobody realizes a separate bottling partner actually manufactures and distributes every single bottle.
